history.label: HISTORICAL SIMULATION 2013-2026 (out of sample, survivors to today): not live and not real money

stages.name: 1 · Read the market
stages.what: Loads daily prices for every NSE stock, the NIFTY index, India VIX, currency and global indices, NSE delivery percentage and futures open interest.
stages.how: Only data public by the close is used; later-published data waits one more trading day. Bad prints are dropped, unadjusted corporate actions are flagged and avoided.

stages.name: 2 · Score every stock
stages.what: ALADIN 1's ensemble of gradient-boosted trees turns about 60 price, volume and market inputs per stock into a 5-day probability of closing higher.
stages.how: Trained only on earlier years and tested on unseen ones; the 5-day score is the one input that ranked next week's winners and losers.

stages.name: 3 · Rank and apply the rule
stages.what: Ranks the liquid stocks (at least Rs 2 crore traded a day). Best 1% get a positive signal, worst 2% a negative one, the rest nothing.
stages.how: The cut-offs were fixed from a 310,816 stock-week study before any live signal existed; the negative band was narrowed from 5% to 2% on 2026-10-09 (picked on 2013-2020, held-out 2021-2026 confirmed it).

stages.name: 4 · Turn rank into a chance
stages.what: Looks up how often stocks at that rank closed higher, and beat the market, in the next 5 trading days.
stages.how: Frequencies from 2013-2026 with 95% intervals; checked out of sample (calibration error 0.015 and 0.010).

stages.name: 5 · Forecast the range
stages.what: For the 500 most-traded stocks, a volatility model plus quantile regression plus a conformal correction gives the 50, 80 and 95% price ranges at 1, 5, 10, 20 and 60 days.
stages.how: The correction is learned on the previous two years and makes the ranges hold their promise: 48-49%, 78-80% and 94-95% of the time out of sample.

stages.name: 6 · Plan the trade and the risk
stages.what: Entry zone, exit level (2 ATR), exit time (5th trading day), round-trip cost, and a position size for your capital capped by risk, position size, liquidity and a fraction of Kelly.
stages.how: A stop does not always fill at its level; sizing reduces the risk of loss, it does not remove it.

stages.name: 7 · Keep a record and learn
stages.what: Writes every forecast and signal to an append-only ledger, scores it when its date arrives, judges 35 trading rules in a nightly test, retires rules that fade, and searches a fixed grammar for new ones.
stages.how: Nothing in the ledger is ever edited; the journal records every change with its evidence.

rule.bull: best 1% of 1264 liquid stocks by the 5-day score

decision_steps: Rank the stock's 5-day score among all liquid stocks
Compare the rank with the fixed cut-offs (best 1%, worst 2%)
Look up the measured chance for that rank
Set the exit level and the 5-day time limit
Size the position for your capital and stand aside if the edge is inside the cost
